text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Talks between Mubarak and Chirac in Paris illustrate their identical belief in the need to achieve just peace in the region. Mubarak says peace talks are going through difficult spell that can be overcome by strong will.

- President to arrive in Washington today amid welcome by Congress and administration. Mubarak to meet press tomorrow and to meet Clinton on Monday. Foreign Minister Moussa says Egypt is a big regional power and that Washington talks will return things to their proper place.
- Arafat briefed Mubarak on his talks with Clinton.
- U.S. veto in Security Council on resolution criticising Israeli settlements.
- Syrian information minister says Mubarak will speak for all Arabs in his meeting with Clinton.
- Economy minister tells al-Ahram that Islamic banks are part of the monetary system and that government is not thinking of closing them down.
- Journey for peace and development -- Mubarak to discuss peace process and economic relations in Paris and Washington.
- Suzanne Mubarak says Unesco medal of hounour for her is an honour for all of Egypt.
- Mahmoud el-Ghohari appointed coach of Egyptian national soccer team.
- Grand Mufti of Egypt says Islam bars cloning.
